findings.title: Privilege-limiting flag 'enforceRequiredRights' is writable through the Live Data update path with only EDIT right, and its value is parsed fail-open
findings.impact: A principal holding only EDIT on a document can disable that document's required-rights enforcement - including by accident, by sending any value other than the exact string "true". Scripts already stored in the document then execute under the unchanged content author's rights instead of the declared, restricted set. Where that author holds script or programming rights, this is a privilege escalation from 'may edit a page' to 'may cause privileged code stored on that page to run'. It is a bypass of a security control, not a data modification.
findings.severity: HIGH (PROVISIONAL - raw researcher output, pipeline not yet complete)

findings.title: Unrestricted property mass assignment: request-shaped map keys select the document field or XObject property to write, with no allowlist
findings.impact: A caller can write any of the four document fields and any declared XObject property on any document it can edit, irrespective of what the live table exposed as editable. Marginal capability is small for 'title', 'content' and 'hidden' - a principal with EDIT can already change those through the ordinary editor - but the same unrestricted dispatch is what carries a caller to the privilege-affecting sink reported separately at line 330, and it makes the editable surface of every live table equal to the whole document model rather than the configured column set.
findings.severity: MEDIUM (PROVISIONAL - raw researcher output, pipeline not yet complete)

findings.title: Documented 'update' API silently creates a new XObject of a caller-chosen class at a caller-chosen index
findings.impact: An update request can attach a new typed object of an arbitrary class to any document the caller can edit. Marginal capability over the checked right is limited - a principal with EDIT can generally attach objects through the ordinary object editor - but the creation is unannounced, is not what the API contract promises, and moves the decision of which classes may be instantiated out of any code that reviewed it.
findings.severity: MEDIUM (PROVISIONAL - raw researcher output, pipeline not yet complete)

findings.title: HTML-conversion target list is caller-controlled and unvalidated: any submitted property can be routed through HTMLConverter with a caller-chosen syntax
findings.impact: The caller chooses which values are rewritten by the HTML-to-wiki-syntax converter and in which syntax, and can silently drop other keys from the same batch update. Stored content can differ from what the editing UI believes it submitted, and the conversion boundary accepts a syntax identifier that was never validated against the set the document actually uses.
findings.severity: LOW (PROVISIONAL - raw researcher output, pipeline not yet complete)

findings.title: Caller-controlled property name and value are written to the application log without neutralization
findings.impact: Forged or split log records that misattribute actions to other principals or hide the attacker's own, plus retention of submitted values in operational logs that typically have a wider audience and a longer life than the document itself.
findings.severity: LOW (PROVISIONAL - raw researcher output, pipeline not yet complete)

findings.title: Unchecked casts and null-unsafe operations on caller-supplied values raise unchecked exceptions outside the API's declared error channel
findings.impact: Malformed or oddly typed input turns a rejected edit into an unhandled server-side error, producing 500-class responses and stack traces instead of the API's defined failure mode, and corrupting the caller's own map along the way.
findings.severity: LOW (PROVISIONAL - raw researcher output, pipeline not yet complete)

findings.title: Every Live Data write is persisted as a minor edit, keeping inline modifications out of default change surfaces
findings.impact: Modifications made through the live table are systematically less visible to watchers, reviewers and moderation queues than the same modifications made through the ordinary editor, weakening the audit trail for a write path that reaches document content and document metadata.
findings.severity: LOW (PROVISIONAL - raw researcher output, pipeline not yet complete)

findings.title: updateXObject returns the pre-update stored value of the overwritten property to its caller
findings.impact: If the returned Optional is surfaced to the requester, a principal holding only EDIT learns the stored representation of any property it overwrites, including property types whose stored value the edit form is designed never to reveal. If the caller discards it, there is no disclosure.
findings.severity: MEDIUM (PROVISIONAL - raw researcher output, pipeline not yet complete)

findings.title: saveDocument sets only the metadata author when replacing document content
findings.impact: If the content author is not refreshed on content replacement: privilege escalation from 'may edit a page' to 'may run code with the previous author's rights'. If the platform refreshes it at save time: no impact, and this is a false positive.
findings.severity: HIGH (PROVISIONAL - raw researcher output, pipeline not yet complete)
